comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the defect is real and this change fixes the reported case. On the base, a cache built under `LC_ALL=C` keeps serving the C order to later `en_US.UTF-8` calls. On the head, each locale gets its own order, and within each locale the output is byte-identical to the base. The first new assertion fails against the base script and passes on the head, including in an environment without `en_US.UTF-8` installed.

Two cases still serve a stale order, because the key hashes locale *names* rather than the collation `sort` actually loads. A smaller point about the `-s` alternative and a correction to the size of the effect follow.

### The key can still match while sort's collation changes

`sort` calls `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` and falls back to byte comparison when that call fails or the named locale cannot be loaded. Neither situation changes `LC_ALL`, `LC_COLLATE` or `LANG`, so the key stays the same:

```text
Same binds, same keymap, one cache directory (head script, --print)

Case A: another category names a missing locale
  1. LANG=en_US.UTF-8  LC_TIME=<missing locale>  -> setlocale fails, C order cached
  2. LANG=en_US.UTF-8  (LC_TIME removed)         -> same key, cached C order served
                                                    fresh build: en_US order

Case B: locale generated after the cache was built
  1. LANG=en_US.UTF-8, locale not generated yet  -> C fallback order cached
  2. same environment, locale now generated       -> same key, cached C order served
                                                    fresh build: en_US order
```

In both cases the served and fresh lists hold the same 227 rows, with 119 of them at different positions. The base behaves the same way, so neither case is a regression. They are gaps in the fix.

**Impact:** narrow. Case A needs an `LC_*` variable (for example an `LC_TIME` line in `/etc/locale.conf`) that names a locale that was never generated. Case B needs a locale generated after the menu first ran. Either way the stale order persists until a bind or the keymap changes.

**Suggested change:** force the collation on the sort that creates the dependency, `LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1n -k2,2` in `prioritize_entries`, and drop the key change. This is locale-independent by construction, removes both cases above, and matches the existing pattern in `bin/omarchy-theme-color`. The trade-off is the one the PR description raises:

| Option | C / C.UTF-8 order | en_US.UTF-8 order | Cases A and B |
|---|---|---|---|
| This PR (key on three variables) | unchanged | unchanged | stale order served |
| `LC_ALL=C sort -k1,1n -k2,2` | unchanged | becomes the C order (119 of 227 rows move) | not affected |

The C order keeps each modifier set together, for example all `SUPER + <key>` rows before `SUPER ALT` and `SUPER CTRL` rows. The en_US order interleaves them because en_US collation ignores the spaces and `+` in a chord. Which order is preferable is a presentation choice. The repository's own ordering assertions already run under `env -i`, so they check the C order.

### `-s` alone does not make the order locale-independent

The description says `-s` makes the order locale-independent outright. `-s` removes only the whole-line last-resort comparison. The `-k2,2` key is still compared with `strcoll` outside C/POSIX (coreutils `sort.c`, `keycompare`). For the shipped binds the second field happens to sort the same in C and en_US, so `-s` gives identical output there. A synthetic run with modifier-less key names (for example `a + A`, `B + A`, `~ + A`) still reorders between C and en_US under `sort -s -k1,1n -k2,2`. `LC_ALL=C` on the sort is needed for full independence.

**Description corrections:** with every bind the shipped Lua config registers (including loop-generated workspace and panel binds, 227 rendered rows), 119 rows change position between `C` and `en_US.UTF-8`, by up to 70 places (for example `SUPER + SLASH` moves from row 105 to 175), rather than 31 rows by up to 4. Also, `refresh_keybindings_cache` keeps a single records file, so alternating between two locales rebuilds on every switch (about 0.1 s per rebuild in the test environment), rather than once per locale.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the pinned head `02d29f7` and base `9c5482c`, plus isolated command-only runs of the real base and head scripts with a stubbed `hyprctl` on coreutils 9.11 and glibc 2.44, with `C`, `C.UTF-8` and `en_US.UTF-8` available. The bind feed was built from the shipped Lua config in Hyprland's reported `__lua` form. It is not a capture of a live `hyprctl binds`, so exact row counts could differ somewhat on a real desktop. The missing-locale and later-generated-locale cases were simulated with a nonexistent locale name and a private `LOCPATH`. The dependency sources read were coreutils `sort.c`, glibc `setlocale`, Hyprland v0.56.2 key parsing and libxkbcommon `xkb_keysym_from_name`. No live desktop, locale transition in a real session or full repository test suite was run.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted cross-checks of each other's single-sourced claims, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
